tracks.legalName: Request to Expunge Criminal Records of an Arrest or Charge Not Resulting in Conviction
tracks.publicName: Expunging an arrest or charge that did not end in a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Arrests and charges not initiated by arrest that ended in acquittal, dismissal, release without charging, or a vacated or reversed conviction may be expunged on petition. Expunge means the records are destroyed or returned and the name is obliterated from official indexes; the circuit court file is impounded rather than destroyed.

exclusions: Minor traffic offenses under § 5.2(a)(3)(B), meaning a petty offense, business offense, or Class C misdemeanor under the Illinois Vehicle Code or a similar local ordinance, unless the petitioner was arrested and released without charging.
The (a)(3)(A) and (a)(3)(C) exclusion lists are keyed to supervision or conviction and do not reach this track.

AOIC instructs users to download the form in Adobe Acrobat or Reader before filling it and to flatten the PDF before e-filing, so any LegalEase output must be delivered pre-flattened.
rules.fees: A circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected. ISP charges nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order. County totals commonly run from roughly $60 to $235; McLean County publishes $136, comprising a $60 filing fee, a $60 state police fee and $16 for four certified copies. Treat every figure as county-specific.
rules.feeWaiver: Supreme Court Rule 298 Application for Waiver of Court Fees. Section 5.2(d)(1) requires no fee where a Rule 298 order has been obtained or the fee is otherwise waived. Section 5.2(d)(10) waives the expungement fee entirely where the same record was previously sealed under this Section.
rules.notice: Notice goes to the State's Attorney or prosecutor, the Illinois State Police, the arresting agency, and for municipal ordinance violations the chief legal officer of the unit of local government that effected the arrest. The objection period is 60 days from service under § 5.2(d)(5)(B). Unless an objection is filed the court shall enter an order granting or denying the petition under § 5.2(d)(6)(B).
rules.service: The circuit court clerk serves, under § 5.2(d)(4). The participant does not serve anyone. Participant-facing instructions must never tell the participant to serve the State's Attorney, ISP, the arresting agency or the chief legal officer.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and verifies the Request. A wet signature is expected.

tracks.legalName: Request to Expunge Criminal Records After Successful Termination of Court Supervision
tracks.publicName: Expunging a case that ended in court supervision you completed

controllingAuthority.summary: Court supervision is not a conviction under § 5.2(a)(1)(C), so a successfully terminated order of supervision routes to expungement rather than sealing. The waiting period runs from satisfactory termination of the supervision itself, not from the last sentence.

exclusions: Supervision for a sexual offense committed against a minor, for DUI under Vehicle Code § 11-501, or for reckless driving under § 11-503 outside the under-25 exception, all under § 5.2(a)(3)(A).
Minor traffic offenses under § 5.2(a)(3)(B) unless the petitioner was arrested and released without charging.

Supervision terminated unsatisfactorily is a conviction under § 5.2(a)(1)(C) unless the unsatisfactory termination is reversed, vacated or modified and any judgment of conviction is reversed or vacated.

waitingPeriods.condition: Supervision under Illinois Vehicle Code §§ 3-707, 3-708, 3-710 or 5-401.3, or a similar local ordinance, or under Criminal Code §§ 11-1.50, 12-3.2 or 12-15, or a similar local ordinance

Supervision on a misdemeanor violation of Vehicle Code § 11-503(a) or a similar local ordinance that occurred before the petitioner reached 25, where the petitioner has no other conviction under § 11-501 or § 11-503
All other offenses

For Alcoholism and Other Drug Dependency Act § 10-102 and Substance Use Disorder Act § 40-10 probation, successful completion additionally requires that the judgment of conviction was vacated.

exclusions: Ordinary probation completed without revocation is a conviction and routes to sealing under § 5.2(c)(2)(D), not to this track.
Minor traffic offenses under § 5.2(a)(3)(B) unless arrested and released without charging.

tracks.publicName: Sealing supervision, qualified probation, probation or a misdemeanor conviction after two years

controllingAuthority.summary: The Clean Slate Act created a two-year sealing bucket effective June 1, 2026, covering successfully completed supervision, qualified probation, conditional discharge or probation completed without revocation, and misdemeanor convictions. The period runs from termination of the petitioner's last sentence in any jurisdiction.

exclusions: Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(i): offenses in Article 11 of the Criminal Code, or a similar local ordinance, except § 11-14 and a misdemeanor violation of § 11-30.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(ii): §§ 11-1.50, 12-3.4, 12-15, 12-30, 26-5 or 48-1, or a similar local ordinance.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(iii): §§ 12-3.1 or 12-3.2, or Stalking No Contact Order Act § 125, or Civil No Contact Order Act § 219, or a similar local ordinance.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(iv): Class A misdemeanors or felony offenses under the Humane Care for Animals Act.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(C)(v): any offense or attempted offense that would subject a person to registration under the Sex Offender Registration Act.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(A): a sexual offense committed against a minor, DUI under Vehicle Code § 11-501, and reckless driving under § 11-503 outside the under-25 exception.
Section 5.2(a)(3)(B): minor traffic offenses unless the petitioner was arrested and released without charging.

controllingAuthority.summary: Any individual may move to vacate and expunge a prior Class 4 felony prostitution conviction, filed with the circuit court, the Chief Judge of that judicial circuit, or a judge designated by the Chief Judge, after completion of any sentence or condition imposed.
